question: How should the preferences of younger investors shape Edward Jones's offerings?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Research finds younger investors prefer to retain a greater degree of control of at least part of their investing lives, while older investors tend to be more advisor-reliant.
items.quote: While older investors tend to be more advisor-reliant, younger investors prefer to retain a greater degree of control of at least part of their investing lives.

items.text: Forty-seven percent of young investors use AI to research companies or markets, 87% are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios, and 65% still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor.

items.text: Younger investors (Gen Z / Millennials) allocate 32 percent of their portfolios to stocks, versus 58 percent for older investors (Gen X / Baby Boomers).

items.text: Millennials and Gen Z allocate three times more of their investment portfolios to alternative investments than older generations, looking beyond traditional stock and bond markets, driving demand for investment real estate, private equity, digital assets, and gold.
items.quote: Millennials and Gen Z are increasingly looking beyond the traditional stock and bond markets to build their wealth and are driving demand for everything from investment real estate and private equity to digital assets and gold.

items.text: For investors aged 21-43, the greatest opportunities for growth are real estate investments (31%), crypto/digital assets (28%), private equity (26%), personal company/brand (24%), direct investment into companies (22%), and companies focused on positive impact (21%).
